analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 10.22.26
key_insights: Risk assets are lower globally. US index futures are down (Nasdaq -170bps, S&P 500 -100bps), Asia is lower across the board (Korea -350bps, Japan -265bps, HK -3%), Europe is -90bps with Euro Tech -190bps, and oil is +2%.

The note cites two catalysts for the move lower: escalating Middle East tensions, and earnings from META, TSLA, LRCX and IBM that did not give the market enough to move higher. The weakness is weighing on the broader AI trade (DRAM -4%, SMH -3%).

META is -3% premarket despite a beat and an above-consensus guide. Feedback says a potential capital raise remains an overhang, and a dual share class structure was announced. FY26 capex guidance was narrowed to $135-145bn from $130-145bn.

META positives: Muse shows about 25% daily engagement, management sees Muse ARPU potentially exceeding the Family of Apps, core advertising grew 26% YoY, and management gave constructive 2027 commentary. Negatives: compute capacity limits how widely Muse can scale (management expects >10x cost-efficiency improvement in the next year), capital intensity stays high, and several youth-related trials are scheduled in the coming months.

LRCX is -7% premarket. Quarterly results were in line with the Street, but guidance disappointed relative to elevated expectations. 4Q revenue guidance of $8.60bn at the midpoint is below GS at $8.87bn and in line with the Street at $8.62bn.

LRCX raised its 2026 wafer fab equipment (WFE) outlook to the mid-$150bn range and gave a preliminary 2027 WFE outlook of over $200bn (up 30%), led by DRAM, then foundry/logic and NAND. Management cited 10 new Tier-1 fabs coming online in 2027 and reiterated confidence in reaching mid-50% gross margins over the medium term.

TSLA is -4% premarket. 3Q26 non-GAAP EPS beat on better gross margin (19.6% vs GS 18.5%), but revenue missed GS by 4% and EBIT of about $718mn missed the Street's $1,473mn. Capex of $4.7bn was well below GS's $8.0bn estimate, and the lower capex plan weighed on the stock.

IBM is -5% premarket despite a solid quarter. 3Q26 revenue was $17.1bn vs about $16.77bn expected, and Software grew 8.7% in constant currency vs about 6.2% expected. Non-GAAP gross margin of 58.5% missed the Street at 59.1% and free cash flow of $3.03bn was below the Street's $3.16bn. Software growth guidance was raised to 7-8%, FY revenue guidance was reiterated at 4-5% constant currency, and FCF guidance rose to about $16.0bn.

TXN is -1% premarket after a beat and an above-consensus guide. 3Q26 gross margin was 64.2% vs Street 61.6% and operating margin was 47.5% vs Street 43.9%. Datacenter revenue rose 20% QoQ and automotive rose 10% QoQ. 4Q EPS guidance of $2.62 at the midpoint is above the Street's $2.30.

SPOT is +5% premarket on in-line Q3'26 results and positive forward commentary. Q3 revenue was EUR4.97bn (+16% YoY) with 306mm premium subscribers and 788mm MAUs. Q4'26 operating income guidance of EUR820mm is above the Street's EUR811mm, and the Q4 premium subscriber guide of 316mm is above the Street's 315mm.

SAP 3Q26 first take: cloud current backlog (CCB) growth was 26% YoY ex-fx vs GS 23.8% and consensus 24.6%. Organic CCB growth of about 25% has not decelerated for three quarters. GS expects a positive share price reaction and consensus forecasts to stay broadly unchanged.

GS published a note on CoreWeave (CRWV) after its 10/19 upgrade, sizing the financing needed to serve the existing backlog and bring the secured 4.2GW of power online. Investors' main question has been the size and viability of future funding needs.

Procore (PCOR): after attending Groundbreak 2026, GS sees the AI roadmap as meaningfully advanced, with 500+ capabilities launched in a year and the roadmap accelerated six months. GS sees about 600bps of implied FY27 margin expansion and reiterates Buy.
Disney (DIS): Orlando International Airport arrivals fell 7% YoY in August 2026, one of GS's intra-quarter demand indicators for the theme parks.

Macro: US 10-year yield is lower at 5.07%. France's 10-year yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2022. Initial jobless claims are due at 8:30am, and WDC reports after the close as the next closely watched AI-complex print.
Street actions: TSLA upgraded to Hold (CLSA), XYZ upgraded to Outperform (BMO), NFLX downgraded to Peer Perform (Wolfe).

market_movers.rationale: CLSA upgraded TSLA to Hold, as listed under Street Actions. No rationale is given in the note.
BMO upgraded XYZ to Outperform, as listed under Street Actions. No rationale is given in the note.
Wolfe downgraded NFLX to Peer Perform, as listed under Street Actions. No rationale is given in the note.
GS upgraded CRWV on 10/19. The follow-up note sizes the financing needed to serve the backlog and bring the secured 4.2GW of power online.
GS reiterates Buy after Groundbreak 2026, citing AI roadmap execution and about 600bps of implied FY27 margin expansion.

earnings_insights: META (reported 10/21 after close): core advertising +26% YoY, FY26 capex guidance narrowed to $135-145bn from $130-145bn. Stock -3% premarket on the capital-raise overhang.

LRCX (reported): revenue $8.22bn reported vs GS $8.21bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $8.18bn. Gross margin 52.4% vs GS 52.6% and Street 52.2%. Systems revenue $5.73bn vs GS $5.36bn. Service revenue $2.49bn vs GS $2.84bn. 4Q guidance: revenue $8.60bn midpoint (GS $8.87bn, Street $8.62bn), operating margin 40.5% (GS 40.7%, Street 39.9%), non-GAAP EPS $2.18-$2.48 (midpoint $2.33 vs GS $2.47, Street $2.34).

TSLA (reported): 3Q26 revenue $28,046mn vs GS $29,330mn, Street (FactSet) $28,057mn and company-compiled consensus $28,341mn. Gross margin including SBC 19.6% vs GS 18.5% and Street 17.5%. EBIT including SBC about $718mn vs GS about $1,043mn and Street $1,473mn. Company-reported non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.48 vs GS $0.44 and Street $0.45. Capex $4.7bn vs GS $8.0bn. FCF $1,531mn.

IBM (reported): 3Q26 revenue $17.1bn vs GS/Street about $16.77bn. EPS from continuing operations $2.95 reported vs GS and Street $2.85. Non-GAAP gross margin 58.5% vs Street 59.1% and GS 59.0%. FCF $3.03bn vs Street $3.16bn. FY26 revenue guidance reiterated at 4-5% constant currency, FY26 FCF guidance about $16.0bn (GS about $15.97bn, Street $15.96bn).

TXN (reported): 3Q26 revenue $6.06bn vs GS $6.06bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $5.89bn. Gross margin 64.2% vs GS 62.4% and Street 61.6%. Operating margin 47.5% vs GS 45.4% and Street 43.9%. EPS $2.62 vs GS $2.51 and Street $2.42. 4Q guidance: revenue $6.05bn midpoint (GS $5.82bn, Street $5.73bn), EPS $2.62 midpoint (GS $2.27, Street $2.30).

SPOT (reported): Q3'26 revenue EUR4.97bn vs GSe EUR4.96bn and consensus EUR4.98bn. Operating income EUR672mm vs GSe EUR670mm and Street EUR673mm. EPS EUR2.52 as printed vs GSe EUR3.22 and Street EUR2.77. Gross margin 33.0%. Q4'26 guidance: revenue EUR5.2bn (GSe EUR5.21bn, Street EUR5.24bn), operating income EUR820mm (GSe EUR791mm, Street EUR811mm), gross margin 33.8%.

SAP (reported): 3Q26 CCB growth 26% YoY ex-fx vs GSe 23.8% and consensus 24.6%. Total revenue growth 12% YoY ex-fx vs GSe and consensus 11%. FCF about EUR1.72bn vs consensus EUR1.66bn. FY26 topline guide moved toward the top end while EBIT guidance is unchanged.
Earnings calendar: pre-open 10/22 BX, CBRE, CMCSA, DGX, HBAN, HON, LMT, NDAQ, NSC, PG, SPOT, UNP and VLO. Post-close 10/22 BE, KN, MXL, RNG, RHI, SSNC, VRSN and WDC. AmEx reports pre-market 10/23.
CMCSA is +1% on better profitability in the quarter.
risk_factors: Middle East escalation involving Iran and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, with oil up 2%.
META capital raise overhang and elevated capital intensity, plus youth-related trials in the coming months.
Elevated expectations for AI semiconductor names, shown by LRCX falling 7% on in-line results and guidance.
CoreWeave funding needs to serve its backlog and bring 4.2GW of power online.
Widening French government bond yields and a US 10-year yield at 5.07%.
geopolitical: Escalating tensions in the Middle East. NYT reported that the US and Israel are drawing up plans for a short, intensive operation after the midterms, and Trump said 'something will happen fairly soon' regarding Iran.
More Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are cited as adding to Middle East tension, alongside crude +2%.
France's 10-year bond yield continued to widen out, above 5% for the first time since 2022, with France lagging in European equities.
